name: Zara Yaqob
shortBio: 17th-century Ethiopian philosopher whose treatise Hatäta (1667) pioneered an independent rationalist epistemology, critiquing religious dogma, asserting universal human equality, and advocating the supremacy of reason.
centralQuestion: Can reason and the light of the heart independently discern truth and moral justice without subjection to sectarian dogma or human tradition?

keyWorks.title: Hatäta (Inquiry)
keyWorks.description: Autobiographical rationalist manifesto written in Ge'ez, advocating the light of reason ('aql) to dismantle religious prejudice and slavery.
